title: Jane Seymour and Anne of Cleves

feedback.correct: Just 11 days after Anne Boleyn was killed, Henry married Jane Seymour. Henry had been interested in Jane since before Anne’s death.
In 1537, Jane Seymour finally gave Henry the son he wanted so badly! Sadly, Jane died in childbirth.

instruction.text: Match each of Henry’s first three wives with how their marriage to Henry ended.

trainers.hint: Select the pictures to find out what they represent.

instruction.text: Look at this image. How do you think Henry felt about his next wife?

b.sound: He was excited to marry her.

atoms.b: Henry’s ((++fourth fork)) wife was Anne of Cleves, who came from a German family.
People thought that her family would make good allies for Henry because they also disagreed with the ((++Catholic Hindu)) Church.

hint.label: Allies
hint.text: An ally is someone who is on your side. Many royal families would try and make new allies by marrying members of their families.

atoms.b: However, Henry said he didn’t like Anne and found her ((++ugly angry)), so he divorced her very quickly.

feedback.finish: Anne of Cleves got quite lucky — as far as Henry’s wives go anyway! After the divorce, Henry and Anne became good friends. She was given lots of houses and was known as the “King’s Beloved Sister”.
